scoring_cases.note: HUD = fires/n_hud (normalized); in_match = fires/n_im (normalized, then HARD-BINARY, never unknown); map-ID = RAW sum(effective_weight x fired) vs identification_threshold. Implementing one formula everywhere breaks two of the three.

phase_cases.name: doubt_holds_mid_match
phase_cases.note: 🔴 THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE GOT WRONG. A split vote mid-match is EMITTED as doubt but does NOT advance the machine, so the internal state stays in_match and the span is NOT shredded into two.

phase_cases.name: score_window_timing
phase_cases.note: Falling edge arms the score window: elapsed is 0 BY DEFINITION on that frame, so a positive duration makes it the FIRST score_screen frame and the window closes once (ts - falling_ts) >= dur.

phase_cases.name: doubt_does_not_stop_the_clock
phase_cases.note: A doubtful frame inside the score window keeps the timer running underneath: the window still closes on time.

phase_cases.name: rising_edge_aborts_score_window
phase_cases.note: A confident in_match inside the score window aborts it and opens a NEW span — which is how back-to-back matches stay two segments.

phase_cases.name: zero_duration_skips_score_screen
phase_cases.note: score_screen_duration_ms = 0 -> the falling edge lands straight in not_in_match; no frame is ever emitted as score_screen.

phase_cases.name: doubt_margin_zero_is_9_13_parity
phase_cases.note: doubt_margin = 0.0 disables doubt entirely and reproduces 9.13's hard-binary behaviour exactly — the same ratios, no doubt emitted.

phase_cases.name: eof_open_span
phase_cases.note: A span still open at the last keyframe is closed at that keyframe, not dropped.

phase_cases.name: doubt_before_any_confident_frame
phase_cases.note: Doubt while the machine has never left not_in_match holds there: a doubtful frame can never OPEN a span.
